rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.7 describe two lysimeter experiments (clayey Vertisol and sandy soil) with lettuce under DI and SDI with nanobubble-oxygenated treated wastewater, with soil O2, CO2 flux, yield and physiological measurements. Q2: Section 3.1 and Table 3 report that average soil air O2 concentration at 10 cm significantly increased (p<0.03) under both DI and SDI with ONB-TWW in both soils (sand 19.2->19.3 and 18.9->19.2%; clay 16->20 and 18->19%); Fig. 2 shows the time series in sand. Q4: Section 3.1 reports the intermediate variable<U+2014>ONB addition raised dissolved O2 in the irrigation water by 14 mg/L (~20 mg O2 per litre), calculated ONB-stored O2 (~0.005 mg/L), and an O2 mass balance against measured CO2 fluxes (ONB water supplied ~1% of daily O-CO2 emissions; Fig. SI-3). Q8: Section 2.3 states that in the clayey soil experiment the continuous O2 sensors got flooded and could not provide accurate readings; the Discussion admits it is hard to explain how such small O2 additions elevated soil air O2 and that mechanisms remain unresolved.
rows.notes: Soil air O2 was measured by two instruments (continuous KE-50 sensors and periodic air sampling with an Apogee O2 meter), but these are the same measurand/method, so Q3 is no; the mass balance does not corroborate the effect. Two soils only, one crop, one site, lysimeter scale (Q5, Q6 no). The calculated requirement (NB number x internal pressure of 1e12-1e13 for a substantial contribution to daily O2 consumption) concerns the mass balance, not a stated condition for the observed aeration effect, so Q7 no. Table 3 gives soil O2 means without SE/SD and no dispersion is visible in the text for the aeration result (SE is given only for physiological parameters in Table 4), so Q9 no. The clayey-soil aeration results are partly re-reported from Baram et al. (2021).

notes: Full text appears complete, though supplementary figures (SI-1 to SI-3) are referenced but not included.
